4) Short-lived credential lifecycle and attestation flow for ephemeral operator access.

Please attach any supporting evidence (escrow letter, provider roster, playbooks). We're on a compliance clock and procurement will require verifiable artifacts for the security files.

Amrita, thanks — we can consolidate and send a verified package. Summary answers below, full artifacts attached.

1) Provider roster: attached spreadsheet (provider-roster-v3.xlsx) lists all operators with role tags (cloud-ops, edge-maintenance, SRE-on-call) and contract status. Internal note: this includes our direct partners and the subcontracted edge operator (EdgeOps Inc.).

2) Escrow: Redwood maintains an escrow deposit with IronVault LLC. Escrow statement (escrow-statement-ironvault.pdf) is attached; it shows the deposit date and the escrow administrator contact. The escrow agreement permits access under an emergency-defined threshold with joint approvals.

3) Failover expectations: our standard production-to-fallback hot-swap window for same-region fallover is typically under 90 seconds for routing and cert rebind; cross-region cold-swap (full reload from escrowed images) is 4–6 hours depending on data egress constraints. We document RTO/RPO bands per workload in the playbook.

4) Ephemeral operator access: short-lived certs are minted via our internal CA with 15-minute TTLs for troubleshooting sessions; attestation requires 2-person approval, ephemeral key wrapping via HSM-backed KMS, and every session is fully recorded and retained for 12 months in our audit store.

Attachments: provider-roster-v3.xlsx; escrow-statement-ironvault.pdf

Amrita — quick technical addendum inline (quoting your questions):

> For the escrow: who is the legal signee on the Redwood side?

Jonas is the exec sponsor listed on the agreement; legal signoff is handled by our General Counsel (Kimberly Park). We can extract and provide the signature page or a countersigned amendment.

> For hot-swap: does the 90s include TLS cert propagation, or is that routing-only?

The 90s SLA is end-to-end for connection routing + handshake readiness for stateless request flows. TLS cert binding and key material rewrap occurs within that window for session-layer handoffs if the failover path uses our short-lived certs. For long-lived client sessions that require rekeying, additional client reconnection time may apply — we measure that separately (typical reconnect 5–30s depending on client).

> For ephemeral access: audit capture details

Audit capture includes: operator identity, cert thumbprint, session start/end timestamps, full command stream (tty recording), API calls made during the session, file-level access events (read/write) with checksums, and a hash-chain tamper-evidence trail. Redactions are applied only for PII in logs; we provide an unredacted evidence bundle under an NDA or court-order. Retention: 12 months default, archival up to 7 years on request.

Attaching: hotfailover-playbook.pdf (contains per-region RTO/RPO tables and the emergency access checklist).

Ben Carter
Sr. Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: hotfailover-playbook.pdf (pdf)]
